Research

Learning systems that respect the physics.

I study how learning can help communication systems recover, adapt, and make decisions—while staying grounded in signal models, hardware limits, and deployment constraints.

Photonic systemsSignal processingAdaptive communicationsEdge intelligence

My longer-term interest is AI-native communication: intelligence woven through the physical layer, link adaptation, embedded execution, and network control.

Featured publication

Learning-enabled signal recovery for optical photonic ADCs

A two-stage learning pipeline reconstructs signals from a nonlinear photonic time-stretch front end without retraining for each sampling rate or input power.

Research map

One signal path, four coupled questions

How do we recover the waveform? How should the link adapt? What can run at the edge? How should the network coordinate? My projects approach these as one connected system.

Physical layer recovery

Photonic ADC calibration, nonlinear distortion correction, optical impairments, modulation, and estimation.

Adaptive signal processing

Blind equalization, carrier-offset estimation, variable-momentum optimization, and reinforcement learning.

Embedded intelligence

Hardware-aware ML, boot flows, flash protection, memory and latency constraints, and dependable execution.

Network-level control

Radio resource management, bandits, graph coloring, safe RL, traffic simulation, and measurement.

Current direction

From post-processing to co-design

The central opportunity is not simply to add an ML block after a receiver. It is to co-design algorithms, sensing, compute, and control so that a communication system can learn from its environment and still remain efficient, interpretable, and safe.
